references.text: In John 8:19 Jesus repeats the same logic: 'If you knew me, you would also know the Father,' as a direct extension of the claim in 7:28 that the Sender is unknown to the listeners.
John 16:3 confirms the theme by stating that 'they do not know the Father,' which is the central conflict line in 7:28 where Jesus points out that the listeners do not know the one who sent him.

John 5:37 mentions that the Father has testified about the Son, but that the listeners have 'never heard his voice or seen his form,' emphasizing the lack of knowledge about the Sender that Jesus highlights in 7:28.

John 12:44-45 links belief in the Son to belief in the Father and states that whoever sees the Son sees the Father, which is the theological opposite of the claim in 7:28 that they do not know the Sender.
